description:
NOVA is an independent team driven by curiosity, creativity, and a passion for space exploration. Our mission is to explore the connections between Earth, the Moon, and Mars by identifying terrestrial locations that resemble extraterrestrial environments. Through scientific research, satellite data, and innovative technology, we aim to turn complex planetary data into meaningful discoveries and new possibilities for future space exploration.
One mind. Infinite possibilities.
summary: TerraTwin is an interactive planetary analog research platform that helps users discover and explore Earth locations that resemble environments on the Moon and Mars. It combines 3D planetary visualization, global analog site exploration, environmental comparisons, research tools, and scientific resources from organizations such as NASA and USGS. TerraTwin aims to make planetary analog research more accessible and support the discovery of Earth environments that can help us better understand and prepare for exploring other worlds.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

TerraTwin is a planetary analog research platform that helps users discover locations on Earth with environmental and geological characteristics similar to those found on the Moon and Mars.

It works by providing an interactive global exploration experience, 3D planetary visualization, analog site information, environmental comparisons, and scientific research resources. Users can explore potential analog locations and investigate their similarities to extraterrestrial environments.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Makes planetary analog research easier and more accessible.
  • Helps researchers and students discover potential Earth analog locations.
  • Connects users with scientific resources from NASA and USGS.
  • Provides interactive 3D planetary exploration.
  • Supports educational activities and research planning.
  • Brings planetary science and geographic exploration together in one platform.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to make planetary exploration research more accessible and help people understand how studying Earth can contribute to exploring other worlds.

TerraTwin aims to support future research, inspire young scientists, encourage scientific collaboration, and help identify environments on Earth that could be useful for studying the Moon and Mars.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We developed TerraTwin using modern web development technologies and 3D visualization tools.

  • HTML5: To build the website structure.
  • CSS3: To design the interface and create a responsive visual experience.
  • JavaScript: To implement interactive features and website functionality.
  • GLB 3D Models: To display interactive planetary models.
  • Visual Studio Code: For writing and developing the code.
  • Vercel: For hosting and deploying the website.
  • NASA and USGS Resources: For scientific information and research references.

No specialized physical hardware was required; the project is software-based.

5. How is your project creative?

TerraTwin brings together planetary exploration, Earth geography, 3D visualization, and scientific research in one interactive platform.

Instead of simply presenting information about the Moon and Mars, it allows users to explore Earth as a laboratory for understanding other worlds.

Its creative approach combines:

  • Interactive planetary models.
  • Global analog site discovery.
  • Scientific research tools.
  • Environmental comparisons.
  • Multiple planetary exploration perspectives.

6. What factors did your team consider?

During development, we considered several important factors:

  1. Scientific Accuracy: Using credible scientific resources and distinguishing verified information from potential analog sites.
  2. Accessibility: Making the platform understandable and useful for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.
  3. User Experience: Creating an intuitive interface with easy navigation.
  4. Visual Exploration: Using 3D models to make planetary environments easier to understand.
  5. Research Value: Providing useful information and resources for further investigation.
  6. Future Development: Designing a platform that can be expanded with additional locations, datasets, and scientific tools.
